newsitem.title: BAHAMAS: Bahamas PM finishes naming cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Bahamas PM finishes naming cabinet.

text.p: Bahamas Prime Minister Hubert Ingraham, whose Free National Movement won a landslide reelection last Friday, has named five additional ministers to his cabinet, officials said on Thursday.

With the eight named on Tuesday when Ingraham was sworn in for his second term, the five named on Wednesday completed the 13-member cabinet. Junior ministers are expected to be named on Thursday evening.

Ingraham named Pierre Dupuch, former minister of agriculture, as the new minister of consumer welfare and aviation. Former state minister of public works Tommy Turnquest, son of Governor General Sir Orville Turnquest, was named the new minister of public works, a post previously held by the prime minister.

James Knowles, a lawyer, was named minister of transport, Earl Deveaux, a former director of the Ministry of Agriculture and a farmer, was named minister of agriculture. And Ronald Knowles was appointed a senator and minister of health.
Ingraham's Free National Movement won a landslide victory in the Bahamas general election on March 14, taking 34 of 40 house seats and 57 percent of the popular vote.

Former Prime Minister Sir Lynden Pindling, who was unseated by Ingraham five years ago, announced his intention to resign as leader of the Progressive Liberal Party after 32 years in that position, in the wake of his party's overwhelming defeat.
